rules.statement: WeakI selected present -e,-st,-ð,-að; dental past -de/-dest/-de/-don. gewęnd- and sęnd- simplify -ndd- to -nd- in the preterite; present d devoices before -st/-ð. gelīefan retains long īe; selected past gelīefde. ætīewan retains w in this selected long-stem system. gemētan contracts the participle dental to gemētt. ge- already belongs to geglęngan/gewęndan/gemētan; these selected forms do not add a second ge-.

WeakII selected present -ie,-ast,-að,-iað; past -ode,-odest,-ode,-odon; imperative singular -a, plural -iað. liccian retains both c letters throughout the selected stem; tilian has one l and gemiltsian has ts. Variant -ige/-ade patterns are unassigned.

StrongV selected four-stem systems: gief/geaf/gēaf/gief, bidd/bæd/bǣd/bed. Prefixes remain part of the attested lexeme: forgiefan/gebiddan. Present gebitst/gebitt simplify the geminate+dental; second singular preterite uses the plural stem, forgēafe/gebǣde.

āhrēosan follows the s-stem strongII pattern: āhrēos/āhrēas/āhrur/āhror; present second/third singular āhrīest, with long īe selected by the Cook umlaut rule. The past plural/second-singular r is lexical grammatical alternation, not an arbitrary ending substitution.

āhębban follows the checked hębban pattern, preserving ā-: āhębbe/āhęfst/āhęfð/āhębbað, preterite āhōf/āhōfe/āhōfon; participle diagnostic āhafen. Double b in the first singular/plural becomes f before the second/third singular ending.

onfōn follows the contracted fōn pattern: onfō/onfēhst/onfēhð/onfōð; preterite onfēng/onfēnge/onfēngon; participle diagnostic onfangen. Receive retains its separately taught dative object, unlike earlier catch+accusative fōn.

Subjunctive singular uses one form for all persons and plural one -n form for all persons. Strong present uses present stem, strong past the preterite plural stem; weak past retains dental stem. forweorðe/forwurde preserves ð:d alternation; ārīse/ārise differs in root-vowel length while prefix ā stays long. Tense/mood labels remain distinct where sęnde or gelīefde are syncretic.

Present base is present stem+-ende, retaining gemination where appropriate. Strong past base uses the fourth stem+-en, selected forceorfende/forcorfen and weorpende/worpen. Weak gemētende/gemētt and geglęngende/geglęnged follow their lexical weakI stems. Selected worpen is the bare base; optional geworpen is a valid alternative under the source participle-prefix rule.
